**The document doesn't say.** I only have the extracted text of the paper, not the Figure 1 image, so the labels inside the diagram aren't available to me. The text also never uses the terms "visited-profile embeddings" or "aggregated user embedding."

The document has no printed page numbers, so the page numbers below are counted from the page breaks, with the title page as page 1.

**History embedding**
- The Figure 1 caption says the history tower "aggregates recent interaction embeddings using positional attention to capture short-term behavioral intent" (p. 6).
- Section 4.3 describes this mechanism. It is a position-aware attention weighting with a learned positional encoding and a learnable attention vector, followed by a weighted sum of the K precomputed clicked-profile embeddings (Eq. 5, p. 5).
- In the experiments, this is called "P-ATT." It is compared against max, mean, GeM and plain attention pooling, and P-ATT scores highest (MAR@100 of 0.450) (Table 2, p. 7).

**User / query embedding**
- The text names no pooling operation for the user's own profile embedding. It says only that the query profile tower encodes the serialized profile text as e_q = f_θ(x_q), sharing an encoder with the document tower (p. 5).
- The final query representation is not described as pooled. It is formed by "normalized additive fusion": the profile and history embeddings are each L2-normalized, added with a learnable weight γ on the history part, and normalized again (Eqs. 3–4, p. 5; Figure 1 caption, p. 6).

If the figure itself labels these components differently, I can't confirm that from this text. You would need to check the figure image directly.
